title: Are ya sittin down? I went to the pier today :O
first_post_text: So I've been havin a few issues sleepin as is normal for me this time of the year, so I took a sleeping pill last night and slept until just before noon. 😳 I was a little surprised my wife didn't wake me up sooner, but her not doing so let me know when I eventually got up that she didn't have anything planned today. I asked her if she wanted to do anything and she said she couldn't think of anything and I suggested since I didn't have any salted minnows in the freezer and haven't for quite some time, maybe WE go for a ride down to the pier and I see if I can catch any for future use. She thought about it and said, "no, but you go ahead. We went out yesterday. Besides it gives you something to do and gives me a chance to do things around here without YOU getting in the way while I do it. In fact, take a rod with you because if you get there and see ppl catching fish and don't have one with ya, you'll be pissed and kickin yerself for not taking one." (she knows me well)🤣 So I packed my gear and went to the pier today. 😱 Got there just after 1pm. Stayed until 5:30pm. Before I left I went next door and let the neighbor know I was going and that IF he decided to make the drive he'd only need a chair as I'd take an extra rod for him just in case. (he never did come down, got busy doing other things) Picked up some worms just in case and used ONE when I put my line in then started trying for minnows. The one worm was the ONLY worm I used today and it did not induce a bite. 🤷‍♂️ Mixed answers when I asked guys trying for bait how they were faring. One said "a couple here, a couple there", the other said "ain't no minnows." but he was using a smaller minnow net. Once I got mine put together I had NO problem at all catching bait with my 6x6 net. I got some for a friend who was getting there the same time I was as well as getting LOTS for myself. I haz salties again for future use. When that might be, I'm not sure. Didn't get skunked either. As soon as I replaced the worms on my hooks with minnows, I started getting bites. Didn't catch much, but I did get a nice smallie. Also saw several other nice or nicer smallies caught, one of which was given to me (two came home and eventually made their way to the neighbor) and a few farm animals as well. Despite not seeing or catching any today, I was told by someone I trust to give me accurate info that the walleye are STILL around the pier as at least one was caught on Thursday around 5pm. All in all a good day. Served its purpose at least. Wanted to catch some bait if I could, and I did, so I'm happy. Catchin a fish, albeit not one I was actively pursuing, was just a bonus. It wouldn't have bothered me had I been skunked tho. I have NEVER fished off the pier this late in the year. I'm normally WELL into hibernation by now, and generally speaking, only one or two people (they know who they are) can get me to come out of hibernation for a day this time of the year. Haven't decided for sure one way or the other, but I might try again just for something to do sometime next week or I might not. It'll depend on how I feel and how I've been sleeping and of course if the weather cooperates and I don't have anything else planned while my wife is at work. (She was on modified duties last week and off the week before with a sprained knee, work related, but she's back to full duty Monday as her knee has healed enough to allow for that) 🙂

title: Burwell 9/14/26 waves 0.6 ft 🤣
first_post_text: Headed down normal time, had to let ourselves in for the boat. Pretty quiet morning,. possibly five boats seen on the water heading out. Had a look at 30, then 35, 40, 45, 50 figured better set up or we'll end up state side. Around 55 things started to show up on the screen so turned left and slowed the descent. 🤨 A few smacks but no hookup so it wasn't all that promising at first. At 56-57 some hooks and bait combined with the boat's presentation to put one, then another and another and so on into the net. Nineteen in total made it to the net, nothing lost, no undesirables, no bows. No monsters, all the fish kept are nice eaters. It was windy, rough with white caps and our quilted shirts stayed on till well into our day. Water was just under 73* , ran closer to 2.0 today which was much more productive than 2.4 and above. 🤔 Another great trip out on Erie. 🌻

title: Burwell 9/17/26
first_post_text: If you are no longer fishing Burwell, why not? This time fished shallow, it was just as productive as the last trip in 56. Never went past (further east of) the 48 flag, didn't notice the 42 flag until near the end of the trip when heading straight shallow. About twenty to the boat, 3 or 4 smalls released to get bigger, another few eaters got lucky and were also let go. One impressive strike which morphed into a 💩 head before appearing at the back of the boat was let go without entering the premises. 🤮 Skitters were terrible at the dock, a few too many flies on the water. Was strange as the breeze should have been enough, maybe due to the distance from shore. Water was just under 72*, speed was varied, the usuals did the damage. title: Can't go Friday but......
first_post_text: So I was reminded we have plans on Friday, so I can't go fishin. BUT.........I didn't have anything in particular planned for today other than payin bills, so I dropped my wife off at 5:40am for her shift then headed to the pier again just because I NEVER go this late in the season and I have a friend who keeps telling me how many fish he was catching this time of the year off the pier last year, so I figured, why not. 🤷‍♂️ Got to the pier at 6:30am and then sat there for an hour waiting for it to get light out because someone left his friggin headlamp and flashlight on the kitchen table this morning where it did him all kinds of good when he got to the pier in the dark this morning. Couldn't see a damn thing. Once it was light enough to see tho, put my rain gear on to break the wind and headed out to 'my spot,' set up my chair, put some water in my bait pail. I had worms with me, but put the minnow net together and started trying to catch some bait. Did that for an hour before I even put my fishin rod together. Put a worm on the bottom hook, minnow on the other two and finally got my line in the water about 8:40ish. Then continued catching minnows. I got lots again. I got my first bite around 9:30, missed it. Checked, took the worm off the bottom hook. Put a minnow on it instead and put it back. Got another bigger hit......missed it......checked, nothing missing, put it back out, kept tryin for bait. This entire time, I was all by myself. Then someone named Bob came out to visit with me. Said he knew it was me because he reads my reports. Hi Bob.👋 🤣 Then I decided since I wasn't havin much luck in 'my spot' where the water was pretty flat due to the protection the pier gives, I moved to the east side of the pier where there was a nice chop from the east wind and dropped my line in there and within a couple minutes, a bite. One and done. Then I caught a sheephead that Bob was kind enough to help me land with my net. Put it back in the water on the other side, replaced the minnow, and put my line back in and maybe 10 minutes later, hooked into something again. Wasn't very big, or didn't feel like it was, and it was NOT a sheephead, but I dunno what it was because it spit the hook before I could see it, and sheephead NEVER spit the hook.😉 Checked the bait, put it back and again about 10 minutes later, maybe, a barely noticable bite, but I noticed and set the hook...........Bob asked if I wanted him to net it for me and initially I wasn't sure, but then I saw it.......and the answer was YES PLEASE!!!.............WALLEYE!!!!.........4lbs. (I weighed it before I slit its throat about an hour later.) Thanks for the assist Bob. 😁All totaled this year that now makes 75 walleye that came home with me throughout the season. 32 given to me, 57 I caught myself, 25 of those off pier. Well over 200 caught off that pier that I know of because I saw them this year.😯 Didn't get another bite after that and called it a day at 1:30pm since I had other things like payin some bills that had to be taken care of before I picked my wife up at 4. Came home, cleaned that walleye, gave half to one neighbor, the other half to another. Considering they KNOW I'm in hibernation by now, they were thrilled I brought them each half of a fish that was caught today. Sorry no photos today, but you all know what a farm animal looks like, and you all know what a walleye looks like no matter what you call it. (Lunch works) I was a little busy trying to get things done before I had to go pick my wife up at 4. Just barely made it 🤣 As I said the other day, there are a couple people who can get me to come out of hibernation, and they know who they are, but with my birthday coming up in a little over a week, and the fact that I've already been out twice within the last week when I NEVER go at this time of year unless one of those I mentioned who can get me to come out, gets in touch with me askin if I wanna go, I don't think it likely I'll be going to the pier again this year, so I'm hibernating now. Have a good winter everyone.

title: Off Topic - Channel 6-8: Early response to the PHP security issue
first_post_text: **Channel 6-8: Early response to the PHP security issue** You may have seen news reports about two serious security flaws in PHP, the software that helps run this forum. Under certain conditions, these flaws could allow an attacker to run code on a vulnerable server without logging in. For background: Associated Press: Rush is on to patch a software vulnerability that could impact 70% of websites worldwide **Channel 6-8 identified the security announcement and acted promptly. The fixes were applied to our server on October 21, 2026, by 12:49 p.m. Eastern time—the same day PHP released them.** We first tested the update on our local test installation, then installed Ubuntu’s security-patched PHP packages on the live OVH server. The web services were restarted so the fixes took effect. Checks afterward confirmed that the forum, media, resources, and supporting services were working. A separate verification at approximately 2 p.m. confirmed that the running PHP service was using the patched software. Later that day, we also strengthened our Cloudflare firewall protection against these attacks. This was a response to an early security warning, rather than a repair prompted by a detected break-in. **The treehouse explanation 🌳** Think of Channel 6-8 as our community treehouse. PHP is part of the framework holding it together. When the builders announced two serious weaknesses, we picked up the warning and got to work that day. These weaknesses could, under certain conditions, let someone interfere with the treehouse without a key or membership. We tested the repairs on our practice treehouse first, then fitted the approved repairs to the real one. Afterward, we checked that the doors opened, the lights worked, and everyone could still use the treehouse. A separate inspection confirmed the repaired parts were actually in use. Cloudflare is our lookout at the gate. We also improved its instructions to help stop suspicious visitors before they reached the treehouse. **Was there evidence of a break-in?** Our review of available server logs, application files, and security indicators found **no evidence of a successful compromise related to these two vulnerabilities**. In treehouse terms, we checked the available footprints, inspected the framework, and looked for unexpected changes. We found no signs of a successful break-in through these weaknesses. That describes what our inspection found; it cannot guarantee that every possible historical event has been accounted for. These repairs address the two vulnerabilities announced on October 21. PHP published additional configuration guidance on October 23; its applicability to our server still needs checking. **Further information** Official PHP announcement and subsequent guidance Cloudflare’s explanation and protections

title: Commercial fishers raise concerns about Erie perch numbers
first_post_text: In regards to my Post last July 18th on “Perch shortage affects local fish fries”. An Oct. 16th Article in the Ontario Out of Doors Magazine. The Ontario Commercial Fisheries’ Association (OCFA) partially blames a high Walleye population for low Perch numbers. Figliomeni said Walleye typically forage on Round Goby and Rainbow Smelt, but those populations have been at low levels, so Walleye have switched to Perch fry. See full article here: **https://tinyurl.com/mwyzr79u** **AI Overview** The Ontario Commercial Fisheries' Association (OCFA) has raised alarms regarding a steep drop in Lake Erie's Yellow Perch population, prompting calls for expanded research and management adjustments. Key Details of the Decline * **Population Drop:** Yellow Perch numbers in Lake Erie have fallen by roughly 20%, hitting lows not seen since the mid-1990s. title: Glasgow Fri Sept 11 and lost a downrigger ball.
first_post_text: With great anticipation took my buddy from orangeville and his 9yr old son out. They've never really fished before so my mind was preoccupied with their having a good time and keeping them safe. I'm setting up my downrigger and put the ball down on the trailer step and forgot about it. Guess it fell off when I was launching. I feel a little stupid 😞. Launch ticket said 11:55am. If anyone reading this happened to come upon a down rigger ball around the east boat ramp, I'd really appreciate it if u can message me. Oh, and it was painted black. We still had a very good time though, albeit without the use of the downrigger. Boated out to 68' and made use of the SE breeze trolling back with the electric. Love that auto pilot. Speed was 1.3mph to 2.0mph. Most hook ups 1.3 - 1.5. 3 rods in hand, 2 of which weighted with inline sinkers and homemade spinners tipped with worms and the 3rd with a weight forward spinner. Had a fourth setup using a 4oz inline sinker dragging a jointed J11. Actually didn't take long to get the first hit - my line lol. I handed the rod to buddy's kid who fought it for a bit and the fish spit it. Too bad cuz it felt like a good one. A while later got another hit and handed to the kid again. Meanwhile my buddy got one on - "double header". Both lost. 😞 I was shaking my head on the inside. Lol. What we should have done was circle back and work that area. Most of the action we had was at 65' - 60' and in the 40's. Final tally, 8 keepers including a 17" that we kept cuz it was the kids first walleye. We also got a 26" and a 26-1/2. The hot blade colours were black with orange strip and black with chartreuse strip counting for 5 in the boat. Haven't used these colours here except @SkinnyTiller reported he was catching using fire tiger pattern. The grey/black J11 accounted for 1 fish. We lost 6 hook ups. The fish were very spunky. The activity on the sonar was predominantly at 40' and above. Hooks between 20' and 40' and the bait balls above that. At one point it looked like the appearance of a thermocline at 35' when we were trolling in the 50' depths but it eventually disappeared. Everyone had a great time. I think they got the bug now. And drop me a message if you found a downrigger ball. Last edited: Sep 14, 2026

title: LPB Oct 14
first_post_text: Lines in at 6:30 up at 14:00. Fished 25-45 fow to stay closer to the north shore and shelter a bit from wind. Still pretty bumpy with waves very close together making boat control a little tough. First fish at 8:15 then 8 to the boat by 9:05. Fish came in bunches, with nothing for up to an hour then a flurry of double headers and singles, then nothing again. Dragged harnesses behind jet divers and dipsys and deep and medium cranks at 1.8-2.4mph. Best was husky jerks 12 and flicker minnow 11 from 125 to 150 behind inline boards. Got several on an old Smithwick deep rouge that was running around 15-20 ft deep. Lots of bait around but the hits came when the screen was mostly blank. Water was 58-60F with a bit of floating weed. Ended the day with 20-25 fish from 17-27" long. Just kept three goldilocks fish with the right size and shape 20-24". Only saw three or four other boats all day. Weather is not looking good for at least a week, so we will see how it goes.

title: LPB Sept 29
first_post_text: Left Port D around 6:00 and headed SE. Stopped in 25fow to have look at the graph and there was lots of life. Debated starting there but figured with calm in the water forecast I would keep going. Stopped at 35fow and then again at 40fow and figured that was far enough. Dropped a couple of glow worm harnesses 75 and 100 ft back behind #1 dipsys around 6:30 and had a limit to the boat by 7:15. Only kept one that was hooked bad. The plan was to start shallow and head deep to see if I could find some rainbows or cohos. Had the lake pretty much to myself until about 8:00-8:30, then the other boats showed up and by the time I got close to deep water there were too many for me to join the crowd. Too tough to navigate when solo. Stayed in the 40-50fow range most of the day, switching between longlining cranks and various spoons and RRF behind dispys. Got a rainbow in 43fow on a spoon, then had another follow as I was ripping a spoon back to the boat as fast as I could crank. Saw it at the last second 5 ft behind the boat before it peeled off. Switched to two spoons for a hours with nothing to show. Back to switching things up between cranks, spoons, worm harnesses, with steady action. Slower, 1.8 - 2.2 mph, seemed to work better again for me. Several double headers including when I was packing up at 2:30. The last hit of the day was another rainbow I think, not sure because I had the other rod in my hand reeling in a walleye. The one in the holder was going nuts but I forgot to lighten the drag when I put the rod back out, so the fish eventually got off. Not sure how many fish I caught, a bunch. Only kept 2 nice 22-24" walleye and the rainbow. The bow had 3" long shad in its belly. Midges and stable flies were annoying, and the gill netters are back in the bay. Saw a line of nets between the elbow and the point, likely along the 70-80 ft contour. I did not get close enough to see if there were any jugs, just saw a couple of end flags and the boat. One of these days I will figure out how to take selfies and post some "action shots".

title: Nanticoke Labour Day
first_post_text: I few weeks ago I took out a my future daughter in-law's younger brother and he had a great time. So much so, that his older brother had been asking if we could go on a fishing trip too. So, on Labour day we went. I couldn't think of a better way to spend the last day of your summer break and I am quite sure they agreed. My son also came along, which was great because he's knows the ropes. I told the boys that I was going to show them how to set lines, land fish, safely unhook them, bleed them, and then they would take over and I would mostly drive. I think they loved it, I didn't land one fish and it was a blast watching them. First stop was our usual area in 60 FOW, there were a ton of marks, but very much to my surprise for the first hour we barely got a sniff. Multiple phantom hits on the riggers, and the dipseys, but nothing landing in the net. We eventually landed a small 14"er which confirmed what I suspected and we headed for 70-80 FOW. The marks looked better, but we got into an area where the bottom 15' was covered in bait. which I also don't like. Nonetheless, we started picking off a few. The catch rate still seemed slow, so I changed our speed from 2.7-2.9 down to 2.5 and that made all the difference. We started catching as usual, had two tripples which got chaotic, it was hilarious. RRF BG worked best on Dipseys, but the riggers also worked. Spoons caught a few. When we got back home, I showed the brothers how to fillet, they got right into it. title: November 2.. November..crazy.
first_post_text: Had a scoop or 2 of minnows left from yeaterday and the bay was near flat so across the bay we went to get back on the perch. Right to the waypoint, on plane all the way there. Drop achor at a smidge after 2pm, send the bait down with the safety off ready for the slightest tap..and waited..and waited...still waiting..WTF. pulled the achor and reset 7,8,9 times, casting and draging off all side of the boat trying to get a sign and not a single hit. Buddy finally pinns a hit and it goes airborn immediately. Huge bronze bomber.. Snapped off at the boat. Keep picking up and dropping and nothing..I finally gets a hit and I lays into! Right to the top of the water instantly, another big smallie.. Popped free at the boat. With a little over an hr left and no sign of perch I makes the call to get on the pike troll to see whats going on. Set out some baits on inline boards, set the speed to 3.5mph. Not even 2mins and one of the reels is screaming. Bronze back again! WTH!! This time we used the net and on to the scale . Continue on with the troll and out of the jumbo smallies and pin a decent pike about 1/3mile from yesterday's hot spot ..then another..then another.."this dont feel pike-ish or bassy". Get it top side and what a surprise, 24" walleye. Zero perch on the day despite our best effort. pulled a couple fish in the closing hr, iced the the pike and the eye. Bronze back released. all 3 fat ass bass were of the same caliber. Didnt catch or hook a single smallie yesterday yet today we tied into 3 of the biggest smallies I seen all year . The rich diverse waters of LPB👌🏽. 10-17fow. Note: had no problem taking a glass boat with inboard motor through the channel at Nanticoke. Stay in the middle of the creek until the break wall of rocks starts then get close, about 20-25ft off the rocks all the way passed the lighthouse,4fow all the way through to the lake. Dont forget on your way back in stay close to the rocks until the steel break wall starts then start getting back to the middle.

title: Oct 25. Inner bay yella's and f18s.
first_post_text: Went in search of perch and found a pile of them but not piles of the size I was after. We managed to to get 2¹/² gallons worth of choice ones for our efforts with a couple scoop of minnows. Tossed every spoon, jigging rap, rippin rap and drop shot plastic combo i had on hand but couldn't sell them on the idea of an artificial bait. Fresh Lively wiggling minnow was the way to the "keepers" hearts. Once we ran through the minnow we put out a few big sticks and super classic f18's. Set the the speed to 3mph started sending them out. No sooner then I got the inline board clipped on we had the 1st long face comming topside.. lost it half way to the boat. Set it out again and instantly had another 1 on Which made it to the boat then the ice box . Reset again and wack! Another long face but a special kind of long face this time, around 33", released . That was a 1st for me @ the inner bay. Lots of weeds fouling the baits constantly, put up with trolling that shit for hr and called it a day. 2½ gallons of yella's. 3/4 pike and 1/1 on the spotty. All in all another great day on the bay.

title: Oct 28 outer LPB
first_post_text: Was supped to take the neighbour with me but he cancelled late, so went solo. I was thinking of not posting because some other very good fishermen i.e., @jammer, @SkinnyTiller, did not fair as well, but hey what is worst thing that could happen, I could be called a bullshidter? Been called worse. Here we go, started just west of the Nanticoke pier at about 6:30 in 25fow. Not much on the screen, but at least there was some protection from the waves. Headed south dragging glow harnesses behind #10 jets. Finally saw some life around 35fow but still no hits. Brought in the baits to check them out and they were fowled with algae. Switch one to a UV storm deep thunderstick and got a good fish right away. Kept switching baits around from harnesses to cranks, to dipsys etc. Hit a period for about 45 min where it was like the middle of August, hard to keep more than one rod in the water. Continued south and baits would get a few fish then go dead, change it out for another bait and it would catch, then go dead. Went through a lot of water with few marks but still go the occasion fish. Fighting a good walleye and the other rod went off with a good run. Landed and released the walleye then landed a nice bull coho with a pretty good hook on it lower jaw. It went on like that for most of the day. Periods of not much action, changing lures and presentation, then a flurry of action. Had another big silver bullet on, a worm harness behind a dipsy. Lots of line peeling and got most of the way to the boat, but when walleye fishing I don't use snubbers and a good headshake behind the boat set it free. Had the three 22-25" walleye I wanted for the day but then another good fish wrapped a hook around its gill and came home for the ride as well. Fished 25-55fow. No real pattern for preferred depth. Speed was 1.8-2.2, with 1.8 best for harnesses but still a lot of hits on cranks at that speed. I have no idea how many I caught, no one would believe me anyway. All females came home. The 2 that had full stomachs had shad between 2" and 5" long. I will try to get some pictures of the lures I used, but flicker minnows and flicker shad 100-125ft behind inline boards did very well. The boards beat the dipsys 5-1 and were hit when there was little or nothing on the screen. My guess is that the shallow fish are being pushed to the side by the boat and do not show up on the screen.

title: Perchin in the Fog-Nov. 12
first_post_text: Well the three of us left home about 10:30, just as the fog was burning off. When we got to the causway at LPB the fog was thick as pea soup, but we figured it wouldn't be long before it was gone on the bay. Stopped bye at Rotten Ronnies and got a good scoop of minnows from Jimmy and we were off to the ramp at Old Cut. Took our time going out as the fog was not letting up, made our way to an waypoint that I have just off the weed bed with only the gps as a guide. Wasn't exactly thrilled about going out that way but we were sure this fog wouldn't last, wrong, it never did get any better. Fished for a couple hours in that general area, but with the fog holding steady we were unwilling to venture much farther. We got into small schools of decent perch and did what we could with them. Kept 27 nice size perch from 8-12" and probably through back about the same. Been a long summer of steady work and it was great to get some R&R time in, the fish in the cooler is an added bonus. Brian (Legend Man)

title: PORT BRUCE- Covering Water, Still Catchin'

title: PORT BRUCE- Fishing Where The Fish Weren't
first_post_text: Launched ~2 with only 2 other trucks in the lot. Split the difference in intel- nice fish being caught in 30fow and good fishing beyond 58fow- and paid the price. Setup over 39fow going downhill, water 71°F and chalky until 41fow with wind and chop out of SW. Ran RRFs and spoons off Dipsys for 50 mins to 48fow then swapped in a jointed, floating Rapala ( blue back). Coaxed one on the Rapala over 49.3fow. Switched 2nd rod to Rigger pulling DHJ12s and Bandits w cheater/spoons and trolled out to 53fow then doubled back with wind and building chop at the stern. Picked off just 1 more on the Rapala back over 48fow. Marked small streaks of bait and decent #s of fish in the top 19' from 39 to ~45fow but very little beyond to 53fow. title: Port Bruce Tuesday August 18th

title: PORT BRUCE- Wormburner From Lambeth Rod and Tackle to the Rescue

Lost 1st fish off Bandit, boated 1st one on Deep Threadfin P10 off Dipsy (84' on 3). Hit a couple slow spells so swapped baits often. title: Port Dover Sept 05
first_post_text: Buddy wanted some fish for a fry. Plan was Stanley but I wasn’t like the chances. Set the alarm for 4am, bouy reading at 1.3 and 1.6 at 5. Texted buddy told him our only option was Dover as it’s off shore there but never fished it or reschedule for another day. Dover it was. Left London at 6 on water for 8. Beautiful marina and ramps were top notch. Figured I read enough reports from here that I could figure something out. Headed down the shoreline until I hit stelco Set up in 47fow and trolled around the shoal. Definitely a different experience with the currents and waves. Set up was 3 dipseys, 2 leadcore and flatline. Tried gold miners, bandits and huskyjerks with and without snap weights but couldn’t get a flatline to fire. Swapped it out for another dipsey. Numerous spoons and bodybaits hit the water. Dipseys were top producer. Leadcore both 5 and 4 chipped in. To rough to circle back on fish. Best depth was 80 down 35ish. Will have to give it another go in better conditions to figure out the flatlines. Hit a couple way points for future reference. Only a cooler picture as buddy took home all the fish. Lil whacker on the end took half the fish. The rest contributed.

title: PORT GLASGOW- 2 Tillers in 1
first_post_text: Looked at a beauty weekend forecast last night and couldn't decide where to fish- another run to Nanticoke or Glasgow. Got text from @CBS shortly after and decided to 'even the score' with Glasgow- hooked up the tiller and we were on the road by 7:30am. Launched before 9, right behind a couple gents in a quarter million dollar boat in search of salmon. Right behind us was a couple backing down their 'new to them' boat, on a roller-trailer.... with the winch strap unhooked 🙄 Boat launched itself, barely avoiding landing on the concrete ramp, wife drops the bowline and a runaway boat is now aimed at the tiller 🤨 Didn't see any of it, turned just as @CBS made a spectacular grab 💪 to prevent collision. Beautiful conditions as we headed downhill SE setting up over 45fow- 2 cranks off boards and RRF/Gibbs off Dipsys. 1st fish came on Wonderbread RRF over 57fow then the action stalled so subbed out both boards for Dipsys. Made it ~ halfway to Rondeau before 2nd fish over 67fow. Almost bumped 70fow with no action so turned and headed uphill with bite resuming over 58fow. Kept to 58fow heading E which was the 'zone'. Pulled the pin 'bout 5:15 with decent swell out of the S but still very pleasant. Very little life on sonar- a few suspended fish or the odd hook hugging bottom. A few worm cleanouts, lost 3 and boated 7 but only came home with 6- one escaped by literally jumping out of the boat! Redfins did most damage- modified Nascar w worm was MVP. Speeds were 2.1-2.4 and Dipsy on 3 with 100' lead produced majority of fish. Water temps consistent ~62°F and conditions were near perfect. title: Puerto Vallarta fishing report November 2026
first_post_text: November is one of the best months to experience Puerto Vallarta fishing, as the Pacific waters off Mexico’s coast welcome an impressive variety of game fish. With warm ocean currents, abundant baitfish, and productive offshore grounds, anglers can expect outstanding opportunities all month long. From trophy-sized marlin and yellowfin tuna to acrobatic dorado and hard-fighting roosterfish, Banderas Bay fishing offers something for every experience level. Whether you’re planning a family outing, a half-day excursion, or a full-day deep-sea adventure, November presents plenty of reasons to book a Puerto Vallarta fishing charter and explore these remarkable waters. Offshore Fishing: Marlin, Yellowfin Tuna & Sailfish For anglers chasing big-game action, November brings excellent offshore fishing and some of the very best fishing we have all year long. The deep Pacific waters around Puerto Vallarta attract several prized pelagic species, making it Mexico’s number one fishing destination. Blue and Black Marlin: The offshore drop-offs and underwater structures surrounding Banderas Bay provide habitat for powerful blue and black marlin. These impressive predators are known for their strength, speed, and spectacular aerial displays. Hooking one is an unforgettable experience that challenges even experienced anglers. Yellowfin Tuna: November is an exciting month to target trophy yellowfin tuna. Often found around offshore banks and areas of concentrated baitfish, these powerful fish deliver long, demanding fights. Anglers hoping to land a true trophy should consider a full-day offshore trip with experienced local captains. Sailfish: Known for their distinctive dorsal fins and incredible speed, sailfish are another exciting target. Their explosive strikes and acrobatic jumps make them a favorite among sportfishing enthusiasts, particularly those practicing catch-and-release fishing. Inshore Fishing: Dorado, Roosterfish & More Not every memorable fishing adventure requires traveling far offshore. The productive waters of Banderas Bay offer plenty of opportunities for anglers interested in shorter trips and diverse catches. We also offer the best fishing rates in Puerto Vallarta. Dorado (Mahi-Mahi): November brings opportunities to encounter colorful dorado, also known as mahi-mahi. Recognized for their vibrant colors and aggressive feeding behavior, these fast-swimming fish provide exciting action on light and medium tackle. Roosterfish: One of the region’s most recognizable inshore species, roosterfish are prized for their distinctive dorsal fins and powerful runs. Rocky coastlines, sandy beaches, and areas near river mouths can provide productive fishing opportunities.Mexico fishing report Other species worth targeting include cubera snapper, jack crevalle, and grouper. These coastal predators offer plenty of variety for anglers looking to experience sport fishing in Puerto Vallarta without committing to a long offshore journey. Where to Fish Around Puerto Vallarta Choosing the right fishing grounds depends on your target species, available time, and ocean conditions. Banderas Bay: Ideal for half-day fishing trips, the bay offers relatively sheltered waters and opportunities to target dorado, smaller tuna, roosterfish, and other inshore species. Corbeteña Rock (La Corbetena): Located approximately 35 miles offshore, this famous underwater pinnacle attracts large pelagic predators, including marlin and yellowfin tuna. It is a popular destination for anglers seeking trophy fishing in Puerto Vallarta. El Banco: Roughly 50 miles offshore, these legendary seamounts are known for their productive waters and potential encounters with large blue marlin, black marlin, and heavyweight tuna. Full-day excursions are generally recommended to make the most of the journey. With productive offshore grounds, diverse inshore species, and exciting big-game opportunities, November is a fantastic time to explore the Pacific coast. Whether you’re hoping to catch a trophy marlin, battle a yellowfin tuna, or enjoy a relaxing day exploring Banderas Bay, Puerto Vallarta offers an unforgettable fishing experience. title: Sept 11 outer LPB
first_post_text: Headed out of Port D a little after 6:00. Fished mostly the 40-50ft depth range with just one trip out 80fow. Tried to avoid the pack which looked to be mostly in the 80-100+ range. Didn't have to deal with many boats except the ones blowing past to deeper water. Pretty steady action from 6:30 to about 10:00 with a a fish every 5-10 min or so and a few double headers. Around 10:00 the bite slowed down when I trolled out to 80fow, the waves calmed a bit and the sun was high and bright. At about 11:30 I was back in the shallower water and slowed down to 1.8mph with green and orange harnesses behind a #1 dipsy on 2.5 setting back 125 back, fishing the bottom 10ft of water. Pretty steady fishing until I pulled lines at 2:30. I kept my self imposed limit of 5, one shy of legal so that I can keep fishing and just in case I get badly hooked fish. The biggest one in the photo is 27", a little bigger than I like to keep. Had one bigger, but she was set back. Toward the end, when I was using up the last worm, I sent out a metallic perch hotlips 175ft. It was the last bait in the water and I had sped up to 2.5mph after reeling the last fish on the harness. Cranking fast to bring the hotlips in felt a bump on the line, thought WTH was that, then another hit and line peeled out for several runs. At the speed that the lure had been moving, 2.5mph plus whatever speed I was cranking, I figured that it must be a rainbow. Nope, a giant 28" drum that must have been channeling its inner blue marlin. Still fun on a ML rod and 15lb braid. * [](https://longpoint.on.ca/threads/sept-11-outer-lpb.98015/) IMG_20260911_174331_218.webp 496.3 KB · Views: 23

title: Off Topic - They're up. Stand by til Sunday for photos and video.
first_post_text: Well, it's that time of year again. My birthday has come and gone, and then a few days later Remembrance Day. While I completely understand there are those who put them up as early as Nov 1, and Veterans have said they fought, and some died, so we have the privilege and freedom to put them up as early as we wish, as I have family who has or is still serving in the Canadian Armed Forces (and some of my American relatives served in their Armed Forces) out of respect, as I have always done, I waited until the Remembrance Day Ceremonies had concluded before I began putting up the outdoor Christmas Decorations so it's done before the weather turns. Usually takes me 3 days. Not sure how, but I managed to get the outdoor stuff up in 2 days this year. Took a day off to rest my old achin back, hips and shoulders, and then while my wife was out this morning, I started on the indoor stuff. It's all up now, 2750 lights and 4 lazers in the yard, 850 around the tree and in the houses of the village inside, (and I have lights left over that I had nowhere to put'em. title: Walleye/Bows - Elbow - Sunday, July 14th
first_post_text: SKUNKED We fished 3.5 hours this morning with 6 rods/3 anglers using riggers, dipseys and boards. Beyond sheephead Albert lost one real big Rainbow that he hooked on a silver/blue NK28 35 feet down in 64 fow. A few anglers I talked to did better but not a whole lot. To be fair neither the Elbow nor the Lighthouse were ever a good bet following easterly winds. Even back in the days when limit catches were the norm we would often have to venture far out into much deeper water to get fish after an easterly. We stayed relatively close to the Elbow Gas Well marker this morning and never went much beyond 90 fow. We'll give the Elbow another chance later this season. People were getting fish but the fishery is far more predictable when we have prevailing winds. It was a nice day for a boat ride and all my lures are now clean.

title: Well, did not expect that!!!
first_post_text: Had lines in outer LPB by 6:30, one worm harness 75ft back behind a #1 dipsy and one flicker minnow 11 in 35fow. Not many marks but managed 8 fat 18-24" walleye by 9:00. Released all but one. At 9:15 the worm harness took a rip and I set the hook into an immovable object. Only it started to move and after a couple of minutes it came to the surface and jumped, at least the front 3ft of it came out of the water. Did not believe it at first but after another a couple more minutes confirmed that it was a muskie. I tie my harnesses with 18lb titanium wire and saw that it had the front hook in the lower lip. Fought it for about 10 minutes up the within 15ft of the boat, then it turns and bit off the wire. All I had was the swivel and 2" of wire. It lingered behind the boat for a while then took off. It was at least 1/2 the width of my 99" wide boat. Pretty fish, and not expected on a harness. Kept fishing until 2:15 and ended the day with 15 walleye (and a close call with a muskie), did not lose count this time. Had a couple doubles and a couple of long periods with no action. Not a lot on the finder, but the planer boards were still hitting. baits 20-25ft down in 35-55fow at 1.8-2.0mph.

title: Yak Attack, Sept 16 afternoon/eve Port Bruce
first_post_text: Big thanks to those the responded to my "Eyes on Pt. Bruce" to add clarity on wind/waves off Port Bruce. Beach launches can add another level of challenge with waves, if any. As it was, when I showed to Bruce beach, slight rollers only. No issue launching at around 2:30 pm. As the plan, was going to focus on shallows. In effect, back to my early roots of yak fishing Erie (and before the pedal drive). Shallow (30' ish) and parrallel to shore. Add to the 'back to roots'....Bruce and Burwell are where I cut my teeth years (over 10 now) yak attacking. Burwell...now screwed due to the upstream launch dude ripping up the sub launch area....and Bruce, due to beach erosion, now with huge steep beech sand dunes. Was great to be back to Bruce...and thanks to Skinny Tiller who lit that fire again for me, here. Anyway, to the report.... Cruised to 35' and set bananas (2 and 3) with harnesses. Pink panties on 2, Greasy Chicken Wing on 3. The screen was FULL, top to bottom. Within minutes, I'm on...and loose my first off #2. 5 or so minutes later...a chunky walleye comes to net off 2. I cruise to 36-37, trying to get a less busy screen (thinking that is a mixed bag of fish causing that screen)....then turn to cruise parrallel west- southwest. Frequent fish on and lands...a range of species. The odd walleye thrown in. Far west of Bruce, and in a dry spell including a bare screen, I turn SE and head a bit deeper running to 42' before coming back around and coming back shallow (36'), now east of Bruce. While out, I see a big pontoon boat that had been sitting my whole time thus far. I thought they were bottom bouncing/jigging...and they were but...they were broken down. I offered to pull em in..>HAH....but they said they had someone coming. Poor dudes. They were there a LONG time before somebody came. Through my time, NUMEROUS fish caught, a handful lost before I make the short...the blessedly short run (compared to my now-usual Erieau DEEP runs) home. In total, landed 8 walleye, lost 3... 5 white perch and 2 sheeps. While I went with 24 worms, I was rationing near the end....hah. MOST action, save 1 walleye, were from the 35-36'. Mix between Greasy Chicken and Nascar (pink panties got retired earlier). Was back at the beach by 7:00 loaded and leaving. Thanks for chatting on the water Skinny Tiller. King Joe Outa Here!
